Performers
Paris Chamber Orchestra (orchestra), René Leibowitz (conductor) Documented

The item lists the Pro Arte Quartet as well; the review shows that the quartet plays Webern’s Op. 5 and Op. 9 on the same LP, not the Symphony. The review describes the orchestra as members of the Orchestre National.

[1] [2]
Work version
Webern’s Symphony, Op. 21, for clarinet, bass clarinet, two horns, harp and strings; the edition and the size of the string section are not stated. Unknown

The 1950 review describes the ensemble as members of the Orchestre National playing as the Paris Chamber Orchestra, but does not say how many string players took part.

[1] [2]
Recorded
Not stated Unknown

The item date, 1950, is the year of the LP release. The review of June 1950 shows only that the LP had appeared by then.

[1] [2]
Place
Not stated Unknown

The ensemble’s name points to Paris; neither source states where the recording was made.

[1] [2]
Label
Dial Records (United States), long-playing record Documented

The review gives “Dial 7, $5.95” for the LP containing the Symphony, the Five Movements, Op. 5, and the Six Bagatelles, Op. 9.

[2]
Catalogue
Dial 7 Documented

The February 1951 issue lists the Symphony as “Dial LP” and refers back to the June 1950 review.

[2] [3]
Matrix, take, sides
Not stated; the Symphony is on side 1 Unknown

The Internet Archive item places the two movements of the Symphony among the tracks of disc 1, side 1; no matrix or take numbers are given.

[1]
Transfer
Internet Archive LP digitisation project; the item lists the collections vinyl_bostonpubliclibrary and vinyl_estate-of-sam-randlett_records Documented

The item metadata names the collections and a scanning-station identifier but no individual transfer engineer.

[1]
Transfer date
Not stated; the item was made public on 14 July 2021 Unknown

The public date of the item is an upload date, not the date of the transfer.

[1]
Processing
Digital rip of the LP, with the tracks divided by the digitiser; the ripping note for side 1 reads “scratchy disc”. Documented

Movement I, on the same side, was not published because a spectrogram of the file shows that its first minutes are dominated by surface noise. Movement II is the cleaner transfer.

[1]
Composition rights
Webern died in 1945, so the work has been in the public domain in the EU and other life-plus-70 countries since 2016. IMSLP lists scans of the 1929 Universal Edition score; its United States status is not established here. Documented

Rights in the composition are stated separately from rights in the recording.

[4]
Recording rights
Rule 3 — territorial EU public domain: first published before 1963; the LP was reviewed in June 1950. Documented

The United States status of a 1950 recording is not established. The Internet Archive item carries no licence label and belongs to the Archive’s “Unlocked Recordings” collection, whose description says works there may already be in the public domain; its metadata has no restriction flag and the MP3 downloads without a login.

[2] [3]

Anton Webern, Symphony, Op. 21, II. Variationen. Paris Chamber Orchestra, René Leibowitz, conductor. Dial 7, reviewed in June 1950. Internet Archive LP digitisation project; item lp_symphony-opus-21_anton-webern-ren-leibowitz-pro-arte-quarte. Territorial EU basis (first published before 1963); US status not established.
